title: TiltBudget - latency vs $ tradeoff heuristics (notes)
content:
Purpose
-----
Quick sketch of a lightweight heuristic (TiltBudget) to allocate latency headroom versus $-savings across three serving configurations. Intended as a one-page collateral for product and SRE to discuss tradeoffs (not a final internal benchmark).

Context and goal
----------------
- We routinely need quick guidance for customers choosing cost vs latency: reserved capacity (low jitter), hosted fp16 (default), and aggressive quantization + tiling prefetched (cost-optimized).
- TiltBudget: assign a small, tunable "tilt" parameter that shifts acceptability of p90/p99 tails vs per-query $ to pick a default config and a fallback chain.

Test harness summary (short)
---------------------------
- Workload: conversational-turns microprofile (avg tokens 120; response generation 80 tokens)
- Concurrency: 128 warm slots, 256 sustained requests/minute; burst tests up to 2k rps for 30s.
- Hardware: A100-80GB baseline for fp16; same node family for quantized/tiling tests.
- Models: open-llama-13b (baseline), same model int8 quantized (post-training quant), and tiled-prefetch runtime (session affinity + KV prefetch).

Key numbers (representative)
----------------------------
Latency percentiles (ms) per single-request generation (end-to-end server-side)
- Baseline (fp16 dense): p50=46, p90=122, p99=358
- Quantized (int8, no tiling): p50=62, p90=168, p99=480
- Tiled + prefetch (fp16 core, prefetch KV/cold-warmed): p50=40, p90=108, p99=312

Compute cost per 1k queries (approx, infra amortized)
- Baseline (fp16): $4.20 / 1k
- Quantized (int8): $2.65 / 1k
- Tiled+prefetch: $3.05 / 1k

Tradeoff snapshot (text chart)
------------------------------
Lat (p90) | $/1k
Baseline     | 122 ms | $$$$
Quantized    | 168 ms | $$
TiledPF     | 108 ms | $$$

ASCII micro-chart (p90 normalized, lower is better):
[baseline] ############## (122)
[quant]    ######################## (168)
[tiling]   ########### (108)

Relative tail risk (p99 / p90)
- Baseline: 2.94x (358/122)
- Quant: 2.86x (480/168)
- Tiling: 2.89x (312/108)
Interpretation: quant saves $ significantly but increases median and p90; tail amplification roughly similar to baseline. Tiling lowers p50/p90 and tail at modest cost.

TiltBudget heuristic (draft)
---------------------------
Inputs: customer SLA target (p90 threshold), cost-sensitivity bucket (high/mid/low), tilt in [ -1, 1 ] where positive tilt favors latency, negative tilt favors cost.
Rule (sketch):
- If p90_target <= 120ms -> prefer tiled-prefetch; if tiled unavailable then baseline fp16; quant only if tilt <= -0.6 and p90_target >= 160ms.
- If cost_bucket == high (cost-sensitive) and tilt <= -0.2 -> quantized primary with baseline fallback for p99 spikes.
- Fallback chain assembled by checking capacity/compatibility and expected cold-penalty (if cold penalty > 80ms, avoid fallback switches during spikes).

Scoring formula (toy):
score_config = w_latency * normalized_p90 + w_cost * normalized_cost + w_tail * normalized_p99delta - tilt * bias
where normalized_* is 0..1 scaled across the three configs, w_latency = 0.5, w_cost=0.35, w_tail=0.15; bias is 0.25 (tilt units). Lower score preferred.

Operational notes and gotchas
-----------------------------
- Quantized int8 showed higher median in our runs; likely due to kernel misc and extra memory copies in our runtime (investigate dev kernel path).
- Tiling depends on warm KV cache; cold-starts amplify p90 if session affinity misses. Need to surface expected cold-warm ratio to customers.
- Cost estimates sensitive to amortization assumptions: reserved vs on-demand GPUs change $ delta by ~10-20%.
- Network egress and serialization overhead (protobuf chunking) can add 6-12ms p50; include client-side delta when advising customers.

Quick decision matrix (for sales/devs)
--------------------------------------
- Low latency priority, small traffic bursts: Tiled+prefetch if available.
- Low cost priority, tolerant of higher p90: Quantized pipeline, limit sessionization.
- Uncertain SLA, mixed traffic: Baseline fp16 as the safe default; enable metric-based rollout to quant/tile with canary.

Next steps / action items
------------------------
- (Lucas) instrument quant kernel path to record copy/mem operations (INF-2319). Target: micro-bench per-kernel by 2028-06-27.
- (Priya) run tiled cold-warm sensitivity sweep (vary warm-hit ratio 0.2 -> 0.9) and capture p90/p99 impact. Deliver CSV + small ascii charts into this doc by 2028-06-25.
- (Ethan) validate cost amortization assumptions across reserved vs hosted and produce a 3-scenario $ sensitivity table by 2028-06-29.

Open questions (for runbook)
---------------------------
- How to expose tilt parameter in Console UI succinctly (single slider? presets: latency-lean, balanced, cost-lean)?
- Should we encode cold-penalty threshold to avoid fallback when spikes are predominantly cold (i.e., prefer no-switch strategy)?
- Does policy need per-route tilt (some routes are notification-style cheap replies, others are deep chat)?

Notes to self
------------
- Keep this doc lightweight; next iteration will migrate the scoring formula into an evaluation notebook and attach the CSVs.
- This is intentionally qualitative—numbers are from a single runset; we should avoid publishing as canonical until we have 3x repeatability and CI gating.

End of sketch.
